title: Acceptance evaluation of an item with a long note history spends its whole evidence-read allowance on recovery and returns no verdict
outcome: An independent acceptance evaluation of an item with a long note and gate history reaches the source and returns a verdict, because evidence recovery is bounded relative to the item's criteria (or the host supplies a criterion-indexed evidence set), instead of exhausting the read allowance before any source or command is inspected.
acceptance: The cause is established from source: how the evaluator's evidence-read allowance and the host's entry_limit paging interact for an item with hundreds of notes and gates, and why recovery consumes the allowance before source inspection and judgment can complete.

A behavioural test with an item carrying a long history (at least 200 notes and gates) shows that the evaluator reaches source inspection and submits a verdict within its allowance, and that evidence named via criterionEvidence or recorded criterion links is read first.
The review pair is clean and the full gate passes on the exact landed input.
